unfold.unfolded: Let $w_1,w_2\in W$. Then the following hold. (1) $G_{w_1,w_2,>0}\cap G^{\mathrm{reg},\mathrm{ss}}\neq\emptyset$. (2) $G_{w_1,w_2,>0}\subset G^{\mathrm{reg},\mathrm{ss}}$ if and only if $\operatorname{supp}(w_1)=\operatorname{supp}(w_2)=I$. (3) Suppose that $G$ is almost simple. Then $G_{w_1,w_2,>0}\subset G^{\mathrm{reg}}$ if and only if $\operatorname{supp}(w_1)=I$ or $\operatorname{supp}(w_2)=I$.
assumed: support of an element of the Weyl group
notes: G_{w_1,w_2,>0}, G^{reg,ss} and G^{reg} are not defined in the context, so they are kept as the paper writes them.
I read the label ss as semisimple and reg as regular, since the context does not define them.
